text: Four years of classes. One grid.
Start with what is already done.
Algebra 1 was taken in middle school, so it counts without taking a seat.
Pick a course, pick a year.
The required sequences go straight down the grid.
For a long chain, look at what has to come first.
Then work backwards: Calculus in twelfth, its chain below it.
Then fill each year to a full load — six credits here.
Four balanced years, and every requirement counted.
Nothing conflicts — only the GPA minimums worth checking.
The whole catalog prints as a PDF, too.
Every course, laid out as a document.
And the plan itself saves as an image.
Fifteen minutes, and a plan to take to your counselor.
